input.query: 论文 Reverse-Engineering Satire 中关于 The Onion 讽刺语料使用的证据、数据集构成与分析结论

output.reason: 证据充分支持所解析问题（the Onion 讽刺语料的使用、数据集构成与分析结论）：c-188a871a6da3d11b36702382 明确讽刺语料为 The Onion 的 9,159 条标题、严肃语料为 9 个新闻网站的 9,000 条标题，并说明数据公开；c-5892e58ce4dcf31d0605c1ef 说明为什么构建对齐语料及反向众包思路，并提到 The Onion 每周 600 条中仅 16 条被采用（BIBREF4）；c-35991441f5d61515d411f14c 说明语义分析结论（脚本对立沿好坏维度、讽刺标题常明示坏的一侧、多为 false-analogy 模板、多处替换需遵循同一对立）；c-897d0ecec345d3bdd8f43c85 总结 Unfun.me 与数据集发布。所有结论均来自证据，未补充常识。

claims.text: The paper's satirical corpus consists of 9,159 headlines published by The Onion.
The serious corpus used alongside the satirical corpus consists of 9,000 headlines drawn from 9 major news websites.

According to the paper, at The Onion only 16 of 600 headlines generated each week (less than 3%) are accepted, which the authors cite as evidence that creating satirical headlines requires a level of creative talent few people have.

The authors observe that removing humor from a satirical headline via small edits is typically straightforward, and that this reverse direction requires much less creativity than crafting the humorous headline in the first place.
The dataset presented is a corpus of aligned pairs of satirical and similar-but-serious-looking headlines, rather than individual texts, collected via the online game Unfun.me.
The data collected via Unfun.me, as well as the code for analyzing it, is made publicly available online.

The aligned-pair corpus is intended to enable analyzing the humor-carrying words that make the difference between serious and funny, at a finer granularity than prior work that compared average satirical headlines to average serious ones.

The paper states that the script opposition invalidating the logical step from P(x) to H(x) must be along dimensions contrasting 'good' vs. 'bad', and that satirical headlines differ from typical jokes in tending to make the 'bad' side explicit.
The paper reports that a large fraction of all headlines from The Onion—and an overwhelming fraction of those in single-substitution pairs—can be analyzed with the false-analogy template.
The paper states that whenever multiple substitutions are applied, they all need to follow the same opposition.

The game generates a type-1 task with probability 1/3 and a type-2 task with probability 2/3, such that two ratings per modified headline can be collected; ratings from task 2 serve as a filter whose precision can be increased by decreasing alpha.

The authors state that the most widely accepted theory of verbal humor is the General Theory of Verbal Humor by Attardo and Raskin, an extension of Raskin's Semantic-Script Theory of Humor, which they summarize when discussing their findings.
